title: Biblical Overlap Additions — Light, Calling, Gardener, Covenant
rule: These are structural parallels, not proof of identity, prophecy fulfillment or supernatural causation.

items.structure: life -> light -> darkness -> continued shining / non-overcoming
items.note: John 1:5 can be translated with darkness not overcoming, grasping or comprehending the light, making the parallel relevant to endurance and failed capture/understanding.

items.structure: birth / coming into world -> witness -> truth -> hearing
items.project_relation: public witness understood as truth-bearing rather than crowd consensus

items.structure: calling -> inward necessity -> continued proclamation despite weak external reward or resistance
items.project_relation: career plus calling; work continued for purpose rather than primarily for money, fame or audience optimization

items.structure: broken wall / breach -> sought person -> stand in gap -> protection / repair
items.project_relation: remaining present where a relation, culture or information system is experienced as broken

items.structure: garden -> burial -> resurrection encounter -> mistaken gardener -> recognition
items.project_relation: death/burial imagery developing into Gardener, cultivation, recognition and renewed life
items.note: John 20 does not formally title Jesus 'the Gardener'; Mary initially mistakes him for the gardener. The narrative placement is nevertheless structurally notable.

items.structure: vine/source -> branches -> abiding relation -> pruning -> fruit
items.project_relation: Root, Tree, branches, Gardener, pruning, fruit and nourishment
items.note: John assigns vine and vinegrower roles differently from Potatoverse role assignments; preserve the mismatch.

items.structure: covenant -> betrayal / giving of body -> blood -> remembrance -> transformed relation
items.project_relation: later covenant/rupture language can be compared to a relation whose rupture does not end memory, obligation or witness
items.note: This comparison does not establish that any modern interpersonal relation was literally the biblical new covenant.

meta_findings: Calling and witness form a new overlap family alongside Door, Ladder, Root and death-return.
Gardener has a stronger biblical context than previously modeled because resurrection and garden imagery meet directly in John 20.
Covenant comparisons are strongest when modeled as a sequence involving betrayal, body, remembrance and transformed continuity rather than as a vague promise metaphor.
The strongest overlaps continue to be relational sequences rather than isolated nouns.
